round_history.retrieved_content:
[DAY1 17:21:30 - DAY1 17:21:59]
I walk around looking at the merchandise. "I don't even drink coffee," I say. Katrina says, "Rum." "I can't buy anything; I don't know much about food either," I say. Lucia asks, "Can I suggest buying some fruit?" Tasha says, "Sure. Tell me if you want to eat anything specific." Lucia says, "Anything, just some fruit." Katrina says, "I want those green grapes." Lucia laughs, "Hahaha, really." "You can too," I say. Katrina says, "The Shine Muscat ones." Tasha says, "Okay." Lucia says, "Fine, I'll eat those too then." Tasha says, "Alright." I turn right and go straight ahead. Tasha says, "We'll buy those." Tasha stops at the nearby beverage area. I ask, "What are you looking at over there?" Tasha asks, "Do you think we should buy one box or two?" Tasha picks up a product and talks about it.

[DAY1 17:22:01 - DAY1 17:22:30]
I push the shopping cart toward Tasha as she holds a box and listens to Alice. Tasha: "One for making a cake and one to eat. I think we can buy two." She puts the box in the cart. "Okay." As we keep picking items, I asks, "We'll eat both? Should we buy two boxes?" Tasha picks another box; I say, "Look at me when I'm talking." Alice grabs a box and hands it to Tasha: "This one. This one's big." I push the cart to Tasha; she says "Okay" and adds that box. "You guys can discuss it." "Why choose this one?" Tasha: "This strawberry is delicious." He points at a box and speaks to me; I point back and talk to Tasha. "No, I mean why this one?" Alice: "Because this one feels white, not very..." Alice continues picking items. Tasha: "He wants to buy this." She points at the box in Alice's hand: "This one is big but there are fewer." Tasha: "Look, even though this one is small, there are many of them." Alice: "Full and ripe." Alice: "Are there many?"

[DAY1 17:22:30 - DAY1 17:22:58]
Alice asks, "Are there many?" Tasha replies, "Yeah, this one has two more rows, this one has two fewer rows." I bend down and pick up items from the shopping cart and hand one to Alice and Tasha. Tasha says, "I eat it often." Alice holds two boxes so we can compare them. I raise my hand and point at a box of merchandise. "This one, this one is blocking," I say. Alice asks, "Hey, is it one row or two rows?" I reach for the box up there and look carefully at the box in my hand. "Is it there or not?" I ask. Tasha replies, "Uh, it's there." Alice says, "Oh, this one has 5 rows, this one has 6 rows." Tasha adds, "Uh, it's one row or two rows," and counts, "This is one row, two rows, three rows, four rows, right, right." "Oh, it's not that bad, right?" I say. Lucia suggests, "Why not ask them?" Alice wonders, "Oh, hmm, so should we get the big one or the small one?" Tasha checks another box in the cart and says, "Definitely the big one." Tasha then takes the box from Alice and puts it in the cart, and we continue comparing the boxes.
